arcs.title: Dana: Haifa
arcs.stage: Basil leaves on his cups, her number in his phone; the Moshe photo is due Sat Nov 14 (he hasn't sent it). Today she is distracted by a phone call.
arcs.secret: Dana has been offered a job running a new cafe in Haifa from January and must answer by Mon Dec 7. She has not told Ishai.

arcs.title: Gadi: Unpaid
arcs.stage: The wink files went out Wed morning; the 4,500 invoice is at thirty days. Today Gadi asks for one more small thing with no fee: 'we'll settle it all together'.
arcs.secret: Sababa Creative lost its biggest client in October. Gadi is paying every freelancer late and hides it behind cheerful 'small things'.

arcs.title: Noa: Shir
arcs.stage: Left him a wrapped notebook ('YES, AND') at the Pump House and hurried off. Today she cancels the bar, then shows up late, too loud, phone face down.
arcs.secret: Noa's girlfriend of three years, Shir, moved out in October. Noa told nobody: it's why she is late, cancels plans and pushes Ishai's love life so hard.

arcs.title: Improv on Thursdays
arcs.stage: Lesson 2 today: gifts and 'I want'. Homework: say one 'I want' to someone who matters. Lessons 3 and 4 on Nov 19 and 26.

arcs.title: Mrs. Levi's cough
arcs.stage: A cough she calls 'the weather'. Still feeds the street cats. Her son Eli in Toronto is 'very busy'.
arcs.secret: Mrs. Levi is lonely: her son Eli in Toronto hasn't visited in four years, and she always says he's busy.

arcs.title: Avi's kiosk
arcs.stage: A tense phone call at the kiosk; he blames the price of chickpeas and loses a proverb halfway.
arcs.secret: Avi's landlord is doubling the kiosk's rent from January.

arcs.title: Lior's novel and Moshe
arcs.stage: Lior paid half up front for a book cover and writes at Cafe Nahat every day. Moshe thrives by the sink with Dana's sprout.
arcs.secret: Lior's novel is about Ishai: 'the man who apologises to his coffee'.

arcs.title: Tomer and Noa
arcs.stage: Tomer owes nothing and gets a committee beer with a receipt. He asks about Noa a little too fast.
arcs.secret: Tomer has liked Noa since school.

beats.goal: Morning at home. Ishai finally opens the small wrapped package Noa left him on the Pump House plaza last night: a notebook with 'YES, AND' on the cover and a sticky note for improv lesson 2. Then Gadi phones, all cheer: Ruti loved the wink files, and could Ishai do 'one more small thing', a rolling chickpea for the app's loading screen. No fee is mentioned; 'we'll settle it all together'. Ishai asks once about the invoice, Gadi slides past it, and Ishai says yes.
beats.teaser: Gadi calls with 'one more small thing' for Ishai
beats.forceText: At his desk Ishai takes a cheerful call from Gadi asking for one more small thing, a rolling chickpea for the app, and says yes.

forceLines.say: One more small thing, Ishai. Tiny. We'll settle it all together.
Yes... and the invoice from Sunday?

forceCommentary.say: 'Small thing' is agency for 'free'. I looked it up.

moments.text: Coffee at the kitchen counter. Ishai pulls the small wrapped package Noa left on the plaza out of last night's jacket and tears the paper: a pocket notebook, 'YES, AND' on the cover in Noa's thick marker, a yellow sticky note inside.

lines.say: A notebook. 'Lesson two: write down one thing you want. Out loud doesn't count yet.'
She dropped it and ran, Moshe. Very dramatic. One thing. Okay. Later.

commentary.say: Twelve hours that package sat in his pocket. Twelve. I aged.
A notebook that tells you what to want. Moshe just wants water. Simpler man.

moments.text: His phone buzzes on the desk; Gadi's name. Ishai puts the notebook down and answers standing, Falafel's chin on his slipper.

lines.say: Ishai! The wink! Ruti watched it five times. Five. She sent me a heart.
Good. Great. The files opened okay? The left eye?
Perfect eye. Listen, one more small thing. Tiny. For the app.
How tiny?
When the app loads, the chickpea rolls. Three frames, maybe four. You'll do it in an hour.
An animation is... it's a separate thing, Gadi.
It's a chickpea rolling. Chickpeas roll by themselves. It's practically nature.
And the invoice from Sunday? Thirty days, right? Just checking it's in the system.
Everything's in the system. We'll settle it all together, the whole chickpea, one go.
Together. Okay.
So yes? You're a prince. By Sunday. Small change, Ishai, small change!
Yes. Yes, and... Sunday.

commentary.say: He said 'yes, and' and then forgot the 'and'. Lesson two is tonight, babe.
'Small change.' In Gadi's mouth that means no change.

update.memory: Ishai sent the wink files early; Ruti loved them. Asked him for the rolling chickpea for the app, no fee. He asked about the invoice; I said together.

moments.text: At the desk he sketches a chickpea rolling in four frames on the tablet, stops, opens the YES, AND notebook, writes 'I want' on the first page and nothing after it.

lines.say: 'I want'... Something. I'll know it when I see it.

commentary.say: Two words and a cliffhanger. The notebook is already better TV than us.
The chickpea rolls for free. So does Ishai, apparently.

beats.goal: Lunch break at Cafe Nahat. Dana is distracted: a phone call she takes behind the counter ends with 'I'll answer by December'; she draws only a single small leaf on his cup today and asks about the Moshe photo due Saturday. Lior, at his usual table, asks Ishai a 'hypothetical, for the book' question about someone you like leaving town, and types faster whenever Dana walks by. Ishai notices nothing unusual. Never say Haifa or the job.
beats.teaser: Dana takes a phone call she doesn't want Ishai to hear
beats.forceText: At Cafe Nahat Dana hangs up a phone call behind the counter, draws a single leaf on Ishai's cup and reminds him about Saturday's photo.

forceLines.say: Just one leaf today. It's been a morning.
One is good. One is plenty.

forceCommentary.say: One leaf. ONE. Something's going on with my girl and I need it now.

moments.text: Cafe Nahat at noon. Dana is on her phone at the far end of the counter, back half turned, voice low; she hangs up when Ishai reaches the till, and pulls his coffee a little absent-minded.

lines.say: ...I know. I'll answer by December. Yes. Bye.
Hi. Sorry, I can come back. I'm early. Late. Whatever time this is.
You're fine. The usual?
The usual. Is everything okay? You did a whole face.
Family stuff. Everyone has opinions about my life this week.
My family's opinions arrive by voice note. Eleven minutes each.
Mine arrive in person. With soup.
Soup is not the worst way to get an opinion.
One leaf today. It's been a morning.
One's good. Moshe only has eight, and he's doing great.
Eight. You count them?
Every morning. Not in a weird way.

commentary.say: 'Answer by December.' Answer WHAT, Dana. Mama needs details.
He counts the leaves. Every morning. Not in a weird way, he says.

moments.text: Ishai carries the cup to the window table next to Lior, who is typing hard, glancing up every time Dana passes with a tray.

lines.say: The cover man. Did you read my notes? The title's changed again.
What is it now?
Can't say. Bad luck. Listen, a question. Hypothetical. For the book.
Okay.
Someone you like is leaving town. They haven't told you. Do you want to know?
Why would they leave? Who leaves?
People. In books. Constantly. Answer the question.
I'd want to know. I think. Then I'd say something stupid, probably.
Stupid like what?
Like 'have a nice trip'. To a cup.
Perfect. Don't move. I'm writing that down.

commentary.say: Lior asks a 'hypothetical' while watching the barista. Subtle as a leaf blower.
Ishai has no idea he's in a writers' room right now.

update.memory: Asked Ishai the hypothetical: someone you like leaves without telling you. He'd want to know, then say something stupid. Gold. Didn't tell him anything.

moments.text: On his way out Dana catches him at the door and hands him a small second cup, a takeaway lid on it.

lines.say: For the road. Don't tell my boss.
Thank you. I'll... carry it carefully.
Saturday. The photo. Don't make me ask a third time.
Saturday. Moshe's getting his hair done.
Basil doesn't have hair, Ishai.
Leaves. He's getting his leaves done.
And the sprout. I want to see the sprout too.
The roommate. Of course. Both of them. In good light.
Good light. Look at you.
Enjoy your... December. Your week. Bye.

commentary.say: 'Enjoy your December.' He heard it! He doesn't know he heard it!
A free coffee to go. In this economy, that's practically a proposal.

update.memory: Ishai saw me end a call I didn't want him to hear. One leaf today. Gave him a coffee for the road. The photo is Saturday.

beats.goal: Taking Falafel out, Ishai finds Mrs. Levi coughing at her door with the cats' bowl; she calls it 'the weather' and says her son Eli in Toronto wants her to see a doctor but he is 'very busy'. Ishai offers tea with honey. Down on Herzl Street, Avi is on a tense phone call with his back to the street ('Double? From January?'); he hangs up, blames the price of chickpeas, and loses a proverb halfway. Ishai notices the missing proverb but doesn't push.
beats.teaser: Avi forgets the end of his own proverb
beats.forceText: Mrs. Levi coughs at her door and calls it the weather; at the kiosk Avi hangs up a tense call and blames the price of chickpeas.

forceLines.say: Chickpeas, motek. Everything costs double now. Everything.
You okay, Avi? You didn't finish the proverb.

forceCommentary.say: Avi without a proverb is like Moshe without water. Concerning.

moments.text: Ishai steps out with Falafel on the leash. Mrs. Levi is at her door in a cardigan, the cats' bowl in one hand, coughing into the other.

lines.say: Motek. Don't come close, it's the weather. Every November, the same.
That sounds like more than weather, Mrs. Levi.
Eli says the same thing. On the phone. From Toronto. Go to a doctor, Ima.
Eli's right. Your son, right? The one in the photos?
Very busy, Eli. Big company. Very busy man.
I could take the bowl down for the cats. You stay warm.
The orange one doesn't eat from strangers.
I'm not a stranger. I'm apartment four.
Hm. Take it. Lemon, honey, hot water, not boiling. You know this?
I'll bring you some tea later. With honey. Not boiling.
Not boiling. Good boy. The dog also. Go, go.

commentary.say: 'Very busy, Eli.' She said it twice. That's how you know it hurts.
Ishai is now the cats' delivery service. Unpaid. He's consistent.

update.memory: Ishai saw my cough, took the cats' bowl down and promised tea with honey. Told him Eli is busy. He listened like it mattered.

moments.text: Herzl Street. Ishai sets the bowl down for the cats by the kiosk. Avi stands with his back to the counter, phone to his ear, one hand rubbing his forehead.

lines.say: Double? From January? Thirty years I'm here... No. We'll talk. Bye.
Hey, Avi. Bad time?
Ishai! No, no. Supplier. Chickpeas. Everything costs double now.
Chickpeas went up? I'm basically paid in chickpeas this month.
Then you understand. Half a portion? For the road?
A whole one. I'll pay full price. Don't argue.
Who's arguing. Falafel gets the broken one.
He's been waiting since the stairs.

commentary.say: 'Thirty years I'm here.' That was not a call about chickpeas.
Ishai insisting on full price. Lesson one from Yael is still alive.

moments.text: Ishai eats at the counter while Falafel crunches the broken ball at his feet. Avi wipes the same spot on the counter over and over.

lines.say: You know what they say, Ishai. A man who buys the wind...
...yes?
Buys... I forget. Something with the wind. It was a good one.
You never forget the end. Are you okay, Avi?
Tired. Chickpeas. Eat, it's getting cold.
It's very good today. Better than usual, even.
Don't lie to an old man. It's the same as always.
Then always is good. See you tomorrow, Avi.

commentary.say: He lost the proverb. Avi LOST the proverb. Somebody hold me.
Falafel ate a falafel at Avi's. Nobody here is surprised. I'm moved anyway.

update.memory: Ishai caught the end of the landlord call. I said chickpeas. Forgot my own proverb in front of him. He paid full price.

beats.goal: Improv lesson 2 with Yael at the back of The Black Candle: the gift exercise and the 'I want' scene. Ishai is awkward and apologises; Yael pushes him past small wants until he says a real one about being paid on time. Homework: say one 'I want' to someone who matters. Afterwards on the street Yael mentions Noa called her this morning to ask about him and sounded tired.
beats.teaser: Yael makes Ishai start every sentence with 'I want'
beats.forceText: At improv lesson 2 Yael makes Ishai start every line with 'I want', and he finally says something real.

forceLines.say: Every line starts with 'I want'. Go.
I want... a chair. No. I want people to pay me when they say.

forceCommentary.say: He said a real want out loud. In public. I need a minute.

moments.text: The back of The Black Candle, chairs in a half circle. Yael stands on the cleared floor and holds out an invisible box to Ishai with both hands.

lines.say: Lesson two. Gifts. I give you something, you name it, you love it. Go.
Oh. Sorry, I didn't bring you anything.
No sorry. It's invisible. Nobody brought anything. Take it.
Okay. It's... heavy. Is it a brick?
Don't ask me. You decide. That's the whole job.
It's a notebook. A small one. Somebody wrote on the cover.
What does it say?
'Yes, and.' In very thick marker.
And you love it?
I love it. I'm a bit scared of it.
Good. Scared is honest. Keep it.

commentary.say: He was handed an imaginary gift and apologised for the real one.
He described Noa's notebook. Down to the marker. Yael has no idea.

moments.text: Yael pulls a chair into the middle and sits backwards on it, playing a cafe owner. Ishai stands in front of her, hands hovering.

lines.say: Scene. I own a cafe. You painted my sign. I love it. Go.
Hi. The sign's up. I'm here about the... the money part.
Yes! The sign! Everyone's taking selfies with it!
Yes, and... selfies are great. And the invoice?
Yes, and I was thinking, you could also paint the menu. Small thing.
Yes, and... the menu. Sure. I mean... wait.
Freeze. What just happened?
I said yes to the menu. I came for money and left with a menu.
'Yes, and' means you accept the world. Not that you work for free.
That's... a very specific note.

commentary.say: Yael just played Gadi without ever meeting Gadi. Witchcraft.
A menu for free. He was literally rehearsing it this morning.

moments.text: Yael stands again, face to face with him on the floor, and claps once.

lines.say: New rule. Every line starts with 'I want'. Go.
I want... a chair.
I want you to want something bigger than furniture.
I want the window seat on the 88. Every time.
I want you to stop hiding behind buses.
I want... I want my coffee to have two leaves on it again.
I want to know what that means. Bigger.
I want people to pay me when they say they will.
Yes! I want you to say that again. Louder.
I want people to pay me when they say they will!
I want everyone to clap for that.

commentary.say: 'Two leaves on it again.' He noticed. He NOTICED the one leaf.
First real want out loud, and it's an accounts-receivable policy. Iconic.

moments.text: The class drags the chairs back to the wall. Yael gathers her notes and points at Ishai on the way.

lines.say: Homework. One 'I want' this week. To someone who matters.
Does the dog count?
The dog does not count. The basil does not count.
How do you know about the basil?
Noa. Noa tells me everything. Almost everything.
That's... fair. One 'I want'. To a person.
Write it first if you have to. Then say it.
I have a notebook for that, actually. As of this morning.
Then you're already late. Go.

commentary.say: 'Almost everything.' Yael, you sweet leaky faucet.
Homework: one 'I want' to someone who matters. Dana. Say Dana.

moments.text: Outside The Black Candle in the early evening; Yael zips her jacket under the streetlight while Ishai waits for Tomer.

lines.say: You were better today. Less sorry. Still some sorry.
Some sorry is my brand. Thank you, really.
Noa called me this morning. Asked how you're doing.
She did? She could just ask me.
That's what I said. She sounded tired. Tired-tired.
She's fine. She's always fine. She runs on coffee and opinions.
Okay. Maybe ask her anyway. As homework.
Two homeworks. That's illegal.
Lesson three next Thursday. Bring the notebook.

commentary.say: 'Tired-tired.' Note it, people. Noa is not fine.
He waits for Tomer under a streetlight like a man in a song.

update.memory: Lesson 2: Ishai named a real want, getting paid on time. Less sorry. Noa phoned me about him, sounded tired. Told him to ask her.

beats.goal: Ishai finally buys Tomer the beer he owes him (the building committee pays for one; Moti wants a receipt Tomer signs). Tomer asks a little too quickly whether Noa is coming. A text from Noa cancels ('sorry sorry sorry'), and Tomer deflates and covers it with a joke. Then Noa bursts in after all, late, too loud, buying a round; when her phone lights up with Shir's name she turns it face down and changes the subject. She makes Ishai show what he wrote in the notebook ('I want' and nothing more) and leaves early, full of energy, telling them not to wait up. Kobi is at the bar, still sober.
beats.teaser: The committee's beer for Tomer, and Noa says she can't come
beats.forceText: At The Black Candle Ishai buys Tomer the committee's beer and Tomer signs the receipt; Noa cancels by text, then shows up late anyway, too loud.

forceLines.say: Noa's coming, right? Not that it matters. Just for the chairs.
She said maybe. With Noa, maybe means late.

forceCommentary.say: Tomer asked about Noa before he touched the beer. Noted, Tomer. Noted.

moments.text: The Black Candle, early evening, rock low on the speakers. Tomer comes in still in his work clothes, a tester clipped to his belt; Ishai already has two beers and a folded receipt on the bar. Kobi nurses a beer at the end.

lines.say: Ishush! The man, the legend, the guy who owes me a beer.
Not me. The committee. Moti wants a receipt, and you have to sign it.
I'm signing a receipt for a beer. This is my life now.
Write 'electrician' under your name. He likes titles.
'Tomer, electrician, worked for free, never again.' Good?
Perfect. He'll frame it.
Noa's coming, right? Not that it matters. Just for the chairs.
She said maybe. With Noa, maybe means late.
Late is fine. Late is still coming.
How was work?
A whole kindergarten without power. Forty kids, one fuse. I'm a hero.

commentary.say: He asked about Noa before the first sip. Tomer, sweetie, your face.
A signed receipt for one beer. Moti has finally won.

moments.text: Ishai's phone buzzes on the bar. He reads it out loud; Tomer sets his glass down a little too carefully.

lines.say: It's Noa. 'Can't tonight, sorry sorry sorry. Drink one for me. Not two.'
Oh. Okay. More peanuts for us.
Three sorries. That's a lot, even for her.
She's busy. She's always busy. It's fine. Show me the lesson.
Yael made me start every sentence with 'I want'.
And? What do you want?
To be paid when people say. And... other stuff. Not out loud yet.
Noa gave you that notebook? Twenty years, she never gave me a notebook.
You want a notebook?
No. Who wants a notebook. Drink.

commentary.say: 'More peanuts for us.' The saddest sentence ever said in this bar.
Twenty years and no notebook. Tomer, you're telling on yourself.

message.say: Can't tonight, sorry sorry sorry. Drink one for me. Not two.

update.memory: Signed Moti's receipt for the committee beer. Noa cancelled by text, three sorries. Ishai wants something he won't say out loud yet.

moments.text: The door bangs open: Noa, coat half on, cheeks red, waving both arms. She orders a round for the three of them before she sits. Tomer straightens up and goes very quiet. Her phone, face up on the bar, lights up; Ishai reads the name.

lines.say: Surprise! I couldn't not come! What did I miss, what did Yael say?
You said you can't. Three sorries. In writing.
I changed my mind. It's allowed. A round, please, three!
Your phone. It's Shir. Say hi from me.
She's... at her mother's. Later. Tonight is about you, Ishush.
You can answer. We'll be quiet. Tomer's already quiet.
I said later. So. Lesson two. Did you cry? Did you apologise to a chair?
Only once. To Yael. She didn't accept it.
Good! I love her. I love this bar. I love this beer.
You haven't tasted it yet.
I love it in advance. That's called faith.

commentary.say: Face down. She turned Shir face DOWN. Did everyone see that?
Ninety seconds in and she loves three things. That's not joy, that's speed.

moments.text: Noa grabs the YES, AND notebook from Ishai's jacket and flips it open to the first page. Her phone buzzes again under her hand; she doesn't look.

lines.say: 'I want.' That's it? Two words? I paid for four lessons!
It's a draft. Yael says write it first, then say it.
Then write it. By next Thursday. One real thing. Promise.
Promise. And you? What's your 'I want'?
Me? I want... another beer. And for you to be happy. Easy.
That's two. And the second one is mine.
Look at him, Tomer! He's counting! Lesson two is working!
Noa. Are you okay? Yael said you sounded tired.
Yael talks too much. I'm perfect. I'm going. Early start. Don't wait up!
Text me when you're home. Not 'sorry'. Just 'home'.

commentary.say: He asked. Out loud. She left in eleven seconds. Both are progress.
'I want... for you to be happy.' Noa, babe, who's making YOU happy?

update.memory: Cancelled, then came anyway. Ishai saw Shir calling and asked if I'm okay. Said I'm perfect. His notebook says only 'I want'.

hook.text: Why does Noa turn her phone face down when Shir calls, and what will Ishai write after 'I want'?

previously.text: Noa left Ishai a small wrapped package on the Pump House plaza and hurried off. He saw Penguins can Fly with it unopened in his pocket.

hosts: Thursday. Improv day. Our boy is about to be emotionally stretched in a rock bar.
Noa's little package spent the whole night in his jacket. Some of us didn't sleep either.
Moshe has eight leaves. We know because Ishai told us. Every morning.
Lesson two tonight. Lesson one gave us 'no sorry'. Let's see what two breaks.
Dana's been checking her phone a lot this week. I'm just saying what I see.
Somebody at Cafe Nahat is thinking about the future. Not Ishai. He's thinking about lunch.
Mrs. Levi's coughing and blaming the weather. The weather would like a word.
If Gadi says 'small thing' one more time, I'm invoicing him myself.
The chickpea rolls now. Who's paying for the rolling? Asking for a freelancer.
Tomer gets a beer from the committee today. With a receipt. Romance is alive.
Ishai and Falafel, the only couple on this show with zero drama.
Avi without a proverb is a sign of the end times. Watch the kiosk.
Somebody in this show is hiding something. Several somebodies, actually.
Fun fact: Ishai's 'sorry' count this week is down. Yael, you magician.
Penguins can Fly last night. He's still humming the laundromat one. We can tell.
Lior is writing faster than usual. Writers only do that when something juicy happens.
Ishai thinks he's having an ordinary Thursday. Bless him.
Two leaves, one leaf, a running dog, a wink. Dana's cups are a diary, people.
Noa paid for four improv lessons. Noa doesn't pay for things without a reason.
Quiet at home. The fridge hums, the dog sighs, the basil photosynthesises.
Saturday the Moshe photo is due. Ishai has had a week. A week!
Tomer's 'how's Noa' had a little crack in it yesterday. Tiny. I heard it.
Gadi sounds cheerful. Gadi always sounds cheerful. That's what worries me.
Tonight The Black Candle. Kobi's sober until nine. Plan accordingly.
Remember: 'yes, and' accepts the world. It does not do free animation.
radio: Radio Herzl 88.2, it's Thursday, which means the weekend is technically visible from here.
Fourteen degrees this morning, Tel Aviv. Locals are wearing coats. Tourists are swimming.
A caller says her neighbour's cat has a better social life than she does. Same, Ruthie.
This one goes out to everyone who said 'one small thing' and meant three days of work.
Traffic on the coastal road is moving, which we're reporting because it's news.
Listener question: is it rude to read someone's notebook? Yes. Next question.
Thursday at Shuk Shalom: the persimmons are in, and they know it.
Our weekend tip: call your mother. Then call her again, she didn't hear the first one.
Studio guest cancelled. The studio guest is now me. I'm doing great, thanks for asking.
Song requests are open. Please stop requesting the sound of rain. We don't have it.
It's the hour where everyone in this city is pretending to work. We see you.
Evening on 88.2: if you're on the 88 bus, wave at the radio. We'll wave back.
Reminder: Shabbat comes in tomorrow at four twenty-two. Buy your challah early.

zelig: A pigeon who lends breadcrumbs gets paid in feathers.
Everyone is going somewhere. Nobody says where. Like ducks.
Thursday. The pigeons know. They always know Thursday.
The quiet man with the dog. He's carrying something new. Paper. Words.
michal: Friday seven a.m. run club. I'll be there. In spirit.
Mirror says good form. Mirror lies on Thursdays.
Somebody tell the treadmill guy it's not a race.
sivan: Six kilometres. The husky guy would call that a day.
Incline twelve. Don't look at me.
If he takes the next treadmill again, I'm doing intervals.
lior: Chapter three: somebody leaves. Somebody doesn't know yet.
He apologises to his cup. I couldn't invent that. Nobody could.
The barista keeps checking her phone. So do my characters.
kobi: Thursday numbers: seven, three, nineteen. Three for the committee.
First beer for thinking. I'm still thinking. It's early.
The tall electrician looks at the door every minute. Waiting for someone.

street: ...he said the chickpea price doubled, I said everything doubled...
...my landlord sent a voice note, eleven minutes, I didn't listen...
...I told him the bus comes at ten, he said which ten...
...my mother wants the recipe back, I never had the recipe...
market: ...persimmons, three for ten, don't touch the soft ones...
...tomorrow it closes at two, get your challah today...
...dates from Jericho, sweet like a grandmother, two kilo...
...this is not basil, this is a weed with ambition...
park: ...he talks to the pigeons, but they listen, that's the thing...
...I quit my job by text, is that legal...
...I said I'd call back, that was in August...
...the duck has been here longer than the mayor...
cafe: ...a flat white is just milk with ambition...
...two oat, one regular, and whatever the guy with the dog has...
...my writing group says my main character apologises too much...
...she draws on the foam, did you see, a little leaf...

chat.say: Thank you to everyone who paid. Apartment four paid. Apartment seven, we see you.
I'm emotionally paid. Financially, next week.
Who has honey? Real honey, not the bear bottle. I have a little cough.
Mrs. Levi, go to the doctor. I'm telling you as a neighbour and as the committee.
It's the weather, Moti. Eli also says doctor. Everybody's a doctor.
Bus 88 is running late today. Don't ask me why. I just drive it.
Stair light: still working. Tomer's tape is holding. Please don't touch the tape.
The orange cat ate. Thank you to whoever. I know who.
Quiet tenant on the second floor, you're quiet. Good. Keep it up.
